title: Daily Health Briefing
intro: Good morning! Today's digest spans your five tracked topics — anti-aging, HIIT for women, pelvic-floor training, integrative options for HER2+/TP53 breast cancer, and sleep. Findings are pulled from recent, reputable sources (PubMed, JAMA Network, NIH/ClinicalTrials.gov, Nature, Frontiers, NEJM, and the AASM); each section links its citations as chips. Informational only — talk to a clinician before acting on anything here.

sections.body:
Theme today: the strongest anti-aging wins remain **boring but proven** (topical retinoids), while the buzzy longevity molecules are still early.

- **mTOR inhibitors (rapamycin/everolimus).** The NIA-backed **RESTOR** dose-finding study (NCT06658093, recruiting since **March 2026** at UT Health San Antonio) is working out *how much* and *how often* to dose rapamycin/everolimus to safely lower mTOR in older adults — and expects the optimal dose to **differ by sex**. Translation: there is still **no established anti-aging benefit** to take off-label; this is early PK/PD groundwork.
- **Urolithin A.** A 2025 randomized, placebo-controlled trial in *Nature Aging* (50 middle-aged adults, 1,000 mg/day for 4 weeks) found UA expanded **less-exhausted, naive-like CD8+ T cells** and boosted immune-cell mitochondrial biogenesis — building on an earlier JAMA Network Open RCT showing gains in **muscle endurance** in older adults. Promising for "inflammaging," but short and small.
- **Taurine.** A 2026 *PLOS One* phase-II protocol will test **3 g/day for 6 months** against HbA1c and biological-aging markers — a trial to watch, not yet a result.
- **Topicals (best evidence).** A 2025 *Scientific Reports* network meta-analysis (23 RCTs, ~3,900 people) ranked **isotretinoin, retinol, and tretinoin** as the only agents with a significant effect on fine wrinkles, with **tretinoin having the most favorable safety profile**. Notably, popular "natural retinol alternative" **bakuchiol did *not* reach statistical significance**.
- **Devices.** Red-light **photobiomodulation** (~630 nm) shows collagen/fibroblast stimulation in small studies, but remains an **emerging** modality without tretinoin's long-term track record.

Practical framing: a nightly **retinoid + sunscreen** still beats most supplements for visible aging; treat longevity pills as experimental.

sections.body:
Recent 2025–2026 evidence keeps HIIT a **time-efficient** cardio and fat-loss tool for women — with a consistent caveat to **pair it with resistance training** for lean mass.

- **Recreationally active women.** A 2025 systematic review & meta-analysis (15 studies, 304 women) in *Scientific Reports* found significant gains in **VO2max/VO2peak** and a drop in **body-fat percentage**, but **no significant change in body mass or fat mass** — expect recomposition and fitness, not big scale moves.
- **Before vs. after menopause.** A meta-analysis (38 studies, 959 women, *Experimental Physiology*) reported HIIT reduced weight and total/abdominal fat, with effects **significant mainly in premenopausal women**; **cycling** protocols outperformed running, and programs **>8 weeks, 3×/week** worked best.
- **Overweight/obesity — how it ranks.** A 2025 network meta-analysis (43 RCTs, 2,315 women) put HIIT among the top options for **fat mass**, but found **no exercise type significantly increased lean mass** vs. control — resistance training ranked most favorably there. So blend the two.
- **Whole-person benefits.** A 2026 *Frontiers in Medicine* RCT in obese female college students (12 weeks, 3×/week) improved body composition **plus** depression/anxiety scores, lipids, fasting glucose, and **sleep quality (PSQI)**.

Bottom line: intensity drives the cardio/fat wins; **add strength work**, favor cycling if joints are cranky, and give it ≥8 weeks.

sections.body:
**Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT)** stays the evidence-based **first-line** treatment for stress urinary incontinence (SUI). This week's studies focus on *whether add-ons help* — and the honest answer is "sometimes, if they improve technique and adherence."

- **Pressure biofeedback helps postpartum SUI.** A multicenter, assessor-blinded RCT in *JAMA Network Open* found a home-based **pressure-mediated biofeedback device + PFMT** was **superior to PFMT alone** for new-onset postpartum SUI, with better self-reported adherence.
- **Electrical stimulation for very weak muscles.** A 2026 double-blind RCT (*Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol*, 42 women with very weak PFMs) found adding **sEMG-triggered intravaginal e-stim** to supervised PFMT produced **earlier, greater, and longer-lasting** strength and continence gains sustained at **12 months** (65% vs 18% reporting meaningful improvement).
- **But add-ons aren't magic.** A 2026 systematic review (21 RCTs, 2,373 women) found biofeedback-assisted PFMT ± e-stim works best with **therapist supervision, tailored/mildly-challenging exercises, ≥8 weeks, and ≥80% adherence** — and a large BMJ RCT (600 women) found routine **EMG biofeedback added no benefit at 24 months**.

Key point: **correct activation, supervision, and consistency** drive results more than any single gadget. Confirm technique with a clinician or biofeedback if you can't isolate the muscles.

sections.topic: Alternative & Integrative Options — HER2+ / TP53 Breast Cancer
sections.body:
"Alternative" is best read as **evidence-based integrative care *alongside* standard treatment** — not instead of it. Two threads stand out for HER2-positive (often TP53/p53-altered) disease.

- **Supplements — mechanism vs. proof.** A 2026 *Frontiers in Oncology* translational review maps **omega-3s, curcumin, quercetin** and others across breast-cancer subtypes, flagging real **bioavailability limits** and possible **interactions with targeted therapy**. Separately, mechanistic work shows **curcumin** can upregulate **p53/Bax** and downregulate **MDM2/Bcl-2** in lab models — but human evidence is early and oral curcumin is poorly absorbed. Coordinate any supplement with your oncology team.
- **Why the TP53 co-mutation matters.** A 2025 preclinical study (PMC/NIH) found **HER2;TP53 co-mutant** tumors are **resistant to neratinib** but stay **sensitive to the TOP1-inhibitor payload in trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd)**; a **neratinib + T-DXd** combination is now in a phase-I trial (NCT05372614).
- **Standard-of-care context (strong data).** **DESTINY-Breast09** (NCT04784715) showed first-line **T-DXd + pertuzumab** extended median PFS to **40.7 vs 26.9 months** vs. the older THP regimen. In early disease with residual cancer, **DESTINY-Breast05** (NEJM) showed adjuvant **T-DXd** cut invasive-disease events vs. T-DM1 (**3-yr iDFS 92.4% vs 83.7%**) — with **interstitial lung disease** as a key monitored risk.

Important framing: much of the "alternative" evidence is early or observational. Use integrative options as **clinician-approved add-ons**, never substitutes for HER2-targeted therapy — and note **germline TP53 (Li-Fraumeni)** carries broader screening implications.

sections.body:
For chronic, restless, or **fragmented** sleep, 2026 guidance still puts **behavioral therapy ahead of pills and supplements**.

- **CBT-I stays first-line.** The AASM's **April 13, 2026** clinical practice guideline on *combination* therapy issued two conditional recommendations: CBT-I **plus** a medication beats **medication alone**, but combination is **not** better than **CBT-I alone** — because CBT-I delivers durable improvement without drug risks. **No single add-on drug** emerged as preferred.
- **Medications, briefly.** Newer **dual orexin receptor antagonists** (lemborexant, daridorexant) are FDA-approved options; use hypnotics at the **lowest effective dose for the shortest duration**, and add them selectively.
- **Supplements, honestly.** A 2025 RCT (*Nature and Science of Sleep*, 155 adults) found **magnesium bisglycinate (250 mg/day)** modestly beat placebo on the Insomnia Severity Index (−3.9 vs −2.3; p=0.049) — but the effect was **small (d≈0.2)** and may be driven by the **glycine** in bisglycinate. A 2026 magnesium-L-threonate trial with Oura-ring tracking found **no objective sleep changes**. AASM continues to **recommend against melatonin** for chronic insomnia (it's most useful for **circadian** issues like jet lag/shift work).

Best-practice habits for restless/disjointed sleep:

1. Keep a **fixed wake time**, even on weekends.
2. Reserve the bed **for sleep only**; keep the room cool, dark, and quiet.
3. Dim lights and cut screens during a wind-down window.
4. If fragmented sleep persists beyond a few weeks, see a provider to **rule out sleep apnea** and consider **CBT-I** (in-person or digital).
